key_drivers.name: U.S. Russia/Iran sanctions act signed
key_drivers.observed: The White House confirmed President Trump signed H.R. 5334 on September 18, authorizing and expanding sanctions, tariffs and prohibitions on Russia and extending Iran sanctions.
key_drivers.interpretation: Moves the prior risk from pending legislation to enacted authority; implementation remains the key uncertainty for actual tariff and oil-flow impact.

key_drivers.name: Saudi Oman-routing scale-up partially mitigates crude disruption
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported Saudi Aramco plans roughly 60 million barrels of Gulf crude exports during September and October using ship-to-ship transfers off Sohar, Oman, about 1-1.5 million bpd.
key_drivers.interpretation: Reduces immediate Saudi crude-supply tail risk but does not normalize Hormuz, Yanbu, pipeline, freight or insurance conditions.

key_drivers.name: Black Sea marine high-risk zone widened
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported London's Joint War Committee expanded its high-risk designation to the entire Black Sea after increased attacks on commercial shipping.
key_drivers.interpretation: Raises persistent war-risk insurance and freight costs for grain, crude and refined-product routes without assuming a specific physical export loss.

key_risks: Enacted U.S. Russia/Iran sanctions authority may tighten Russian energy flows or create secondary tariff risk depending on implementation.
Hormuz traffic remains severely impaired despite Saudi Oman-routing mitigation.
Black Sea commercial-shipping insurance risk has broadened.
